newsitem.title: CHINA: China paper urges timely stock information release.
newsitem.headline: China paper urges timely stock information release.

text.p: An official newspaper on Saturday said stock information release by Chinese listed firms lagged far behind that of companies on the world's mature markets and must be improved.
The China Securities newspaper said Chinese firms in most cases did not give explanations when their share prices fluctuated extraordinarily, only denying rumours when they became widespread.
It said China's securities rules on stock information release were imperfect and should be revised to indicate clearly in what circumstances a firm should issue statements.
Many Chinese firms release crucial information, such as reversals in a company's performance, through news reports instead of in company statements, the newspaper said.

This is unfair because such releases, unlike company statements, do not lead to the suspension of a firm's shares or bring the changes to the attention of all investors, it said. China currently has no securities law. The securities markets are subject to various regulations released by Beijing, regional governments and the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges themselves.
